title: Chapter 10 Quiz
description: Test your knowledge of model saving, TensorFlow Serving, TFLite conversion, and mobile deployment!

questions.question: Which format is the standard for serving TensorFlow models in production?
questions.explanation: SavedModel is the universal format for serving, exporting to TFLite, and TF.js.

questions.question: `model.save('my_model')` creates a single HDF5 file.
questions.explanation: By default in TF2, `model.save()` creates a SavedModel directory, not an HDF5 file. To save as HDF5, use `model.save('model.h5')`.

questions.question: What does `model.save_weights('ckpt')` store?
questions.explanation: `save_weights` saves the weight values only, not the model structure.

questions.question: To load a Keras SavedModel, you use `tf.keras.models._____('path')`.
questions.explanation: The function is `tf.keras.models.load_model`.

questions.question: What is TensorFlow Serving?
options: A Python library for training models
A high‑performance serving system for ML models
questions.explanation: TF Serving is a C++ server that serves models via gRPC/REST.

questions.question: TensorFlow Serving supports both gRPC and REST APIs.
questions.explanation: It exposes both gRPC and HTTP REST endpoints for flexibility.

questions.question: What is a serving signature?
options: A definition of the input and output tensors for inference
questions.explanation: The signature tells the server what inputs to expect and outputs to return.

questions.question: How does TensorFlow Serving handle multiple model versions?
options: It doesn't; only one version can be loaded
It automatically serves the highest version number unless specified
questions.explanation: By default, the latest (highest) version is served; you can request a specific version in the URL.

questions.question: The tool to inspect a SavedModel from the command line is `_____`.
questions.explanation: `saved_model_cli show --dir ...` displays signatures and graph info.

questions.question: Why use TensorFlow Lite?
options: To run models on mobile and embedded devices with low latency and small size
To serve models in a data center
questions.explanation: TFLite is optimized for on‑device inference with a lightweight interpreter.

questions.question: Which class is used to convert a SavedModel to TFLite?
questions.explanation: `tf.lite.TFLiteConverter` handles conversion.

questions.question: Quantization from float32 to int8 always increases model accuracy.
questions.explanation: Quantization reduces precision, which may cause a small accuracy drop, but the model becomes much smaller and faster.

questions.question: What is needed for full integer quantization (int8)?
questions.explanation: A small set of representative samples is used to determine quantization ranges.

questions.question: Which TFLite optimization applies dynamic range quantization?
questions.explanation: `tf.lite.Optimize.DEFAULT` enables dynamic range quantization (weights quantized to 8 bits).

questions.question: How do you run inference with a TFLite model in Python?
questions.explanation: The `Interpreter` class loads a .tflite model and provides methods to set inputs and get outputs.

questions.question: TFLite models can run on a Raspberry Pi or a microcontroller.
questions.explanation: TFLite supports even microcontrollers via TensorFlow Lite for Microcontrollers.

questions.question: Which delegate would you use to accelerate TFLite on Android GPU?
questions.explanation: The GPU delegate offloads computation to the mobile GPU.

questions.question: What is the advantage of running a model on‑device instead of on a server?
questions.explanation: On‑device inference eliminates network latency and works without connectivity.

questions.question: In TFLite, to ensure inputs and outputs are uint8, set `converter.inference_input_type = tf._____`.
questions.explanation: For full integer quantization, input/output type can be uint8 or int8.

questions.question: Which is NOT a step in deploying a TFLite model to an Android app?
options: Write TensorFlow training code in Java
questions.explanation: Training is done in Python; the Android app only runs inference, no training code.
